summary: Fuel curve: Ta'u's reported 109,500 gal/yr of diesel implies 1,263,778 kWh/yr on our fuel curve; the separately reported figure is 1,300,000 kWh (-2.8%).
As built (1.41 MW + 6 MWh): our engine gives 99.7% solar in a typical year (98.9% in the worst of 20), saving 109,114 gal/yr; published: almost 100% solar, ~109,500 gal/yr.

Our optimiser would build 942 kW + 2673 kWh for a 91% diesel cut; on our prices the as-built system costs 66% more over 20 years to remove the last 9% of diesel. A fair choice for an island that wanted to stop fuel shipments; the engine puts a price on it.

Where we differ: the battery alone covers 1.3 days of average load, not the advertised 3; in the darkest 3 days of 20 years (starting from the charge normal running left, generator off) the whole island stays powered 46 of 72 hours (21% of normal sun). Refill from 20% on a clear day: 9 h from sunrise (advertised: 7 h).
